Investigation of the Potential of Selected Food-Derived Antioxidants to Bind and Stabilise the Bioactive Blue Protein C-Phycocyanin from Cyanobacteria Spirulina
Nikola Gligorijević
Nikola Gligorijević
Blue C-phycocyanin (C-PC), the major Spirulina protein with innumerable health-promoting benefits, is an attractive colourant and food supplement. A crucial obstacle to its more extensive use is its relatively low stability.
This study aimed to screen various food-derived ligands for their ability to bind and stabilise C-PC, utilising spectroscopic techniques and molecular docking.
Selected ligands did not affect the secondary structure content, but they induced changes in the tertiary protein structure in the CD study. A fluorescence-based thermal stability assay demonstrated quercetin and coenzyme Q 10 increased the C-PC melting point by nearly 5 °C.
Our study identified food-derived ligands that interact with C-PC and improve its thermal stability, indicating their potential as stabilising agents for C-PC in the food industry.
A vital drawback to the broader utilisation of C-PC on an industrial scale is its low stability during food processing since C-PC from Spirulina is sensitive to high temperatures, light and pH. In solution, C-PC’s melting point (T m ) is about 50 °C; above it, denaturation occurs [ 13 ].
Quercetin ( A ), resveratrol ( B ), coenzyme Q 10 ( C ), dihydrolipoic acid ( D ), menthol ( E ), vanillin ( F ), 3,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid ( G ), trans -ferulic acid ( H ), syringic acid ( I ), vanillic acid ( J ), caffeic acid ( K ) and ellagic acid ( L ).
The thermal stability analysis of C-PC alone and in the presence of the tested ligands is presented in Figure 8 . The effects of quercetin and coenzyme Q 10 on the thermal stability of C-PC were studied by monitoring the ratio of protein fluorescence at 335 and 345 nm (excitation at 280 nm).
C-PC has an intense blue colour originating from its prosthetic group, PCB, which is very hard to find in nature [ 30 ]. Due to its attractive appearance, C-PC has excellent potential to be utilised as a food colourant.
It was shown that quercetin and coenzyme Q 10 increase its T m by nearly 5 °C. C-PC’s thermal stability depends on its purity, with a reagent-grade protein having lower stability than a food-grade one [ 38 ]. Enriching crude Spirulina extract with the mentioned antioxidants could improve the thermal stability of C-PC even further.
The binding potential of 12 food-derived antioxidants, including quercetin, resveratrol, coenzyme Q 10 , dihydrolipoic acid, menthol, vanillin, 3,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid, trans -ferulic acid, syringic acid, vanillic acid, caffeic acid and ellagic acid ( Figure 1 ), for C-PC was tested.
This study probed the potential of various food-derived antioxidants to bind and stabilise C-phycocyanin (C-PC), a major protein in the cyanobacteria Arthrospira platensis , also known as Spirulina.

Abstract
The present innovation relates to the formulation and development of a functional beverage of pectin–adjuvanted spirulina, designed to deliver enhanced nutritional, antioxidant, and therapeutic properties for human health.
The invention combines natural pectin (0.5–1.5% w/v), derived from citrus or apple sources, with Spirulina platensis extract (2–5% w/v), enriched with proteins, phycocyanin, vitamins, and essential minerals. The synergistic formulation stabilizes bioactive compounds, improves palatability, and enhances bioavailability.
The beverage base consists of purified water (85–90%), natural sweeteners such as stevia (0.2–0.5%), and citric acid (0.1–0.3%) to maintain pH between 6.2 and 6.8 for optimal stability.
Experimental trials indicate that pectin acts as an adjuvant by forming a colloidal matrix around spirulina molecules, thereby protecting phycocyanin and chlorophyll-a from thermal and oxidative degradation during pasteurization (70°C for 10 minutes).
Stability tests showed that over 90% of antioxidant activity was retained after 30 days of storage at 4°C, compared to 65% in control spirulina drinks without pectin. The protein retention was recorded at 18.2 ± 0.5 g/L, and total phenolic content increased by 22% due to synergistic interaction between pectin and spirulina metabolites.
The beverage exhibits potent antioxidant capacity (IC50 = 45 µg/mL in DPPH assay) and immunomodulatory potential demonstrated through in vitro macrophage stimulation assays.
The developed formulation provides a ready-to-drink nutraceutical suitable for diabetic, vegan, and health-conscious consumers, with extended shelf life and enhanced nutrient stability.
This specific ratio ensures stabilization of bioactive compounds and creates a synergistic nutritional effect not observed in conventional spirulina beverages.

This claim highlights the superior thermal and oxidative stability achieved through pectin’s encapsulating properties, protecting phycocyanin and chlorophyll-a pigments.

The formulation balance between spirulina, pectin, and citric acid enhances color retention, antioxidant potency, and product consistency.

Claim 6: Long-Term Physical and Chemical StabilityThe beverage demonstrates no sedimentation, phase separation, or pigment loss during 30 days of storage, with stable viscosity (1.45–1.60 cP). This proves the structural integrity and colloidal stability provided by pectin as a functional stabilizer.
